question: A spell's effect creates a delayed trigger that says 'when this creature leaves the battlefield, do something.' But the creature leaves the battlefield before that spell actually finishes resolving and creates the delayed trigger. Does the delayed ability still trigger once the creature is gone?
workedSolution: Part of an effect reads “When this creature leaves the battlefield,” but the creature in question leaves the battlefield before the spell or ability creating the effect resolves. In this case, the delayed ability never triggers.

whyHard: A delayed triggered ability doesn't exist until the spell or ability that creates it actually resolves -- it can't retroactively trigger off an event that already happened before it was created, even though the plain English of "when this creature leaves" reads as if it should still catch a leave that already occurred.
